11		bmanifest "github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli/internal/manifest"
12	)
13	
14	// integrity.go cross-checks the manifest's declared fact source against
15	// the facts the store can actually produce — both HOW MANY it produces and
16	// WHICH ones, because a corruption can leave the first right while destroying
17	// the second (see COUNTS ARE NOT ENOUGH below).
18	//
19	// sources.facts in the manifest is a CLAIM: "this brain holds N facts". Every
20	// health surface printed that claim as though it were an observation, and
21	// nothing ever compared it to the store. A facts.ndjson that had gone lossy —
22	// a line overwritten with valid JSON that is not a fact record, a truncated
23	// file, a botched hand edit — therefore kept reporting N on `status`, `doctor`
24	// and `facts map` while recall returned fewer, `get fact:<id>` said "not
25	// found", and `search` volunteered that the answer "may genuinely not be in
26	// the brain". For a durable-memory product that last line converts silent data
27	// loss into an affirmative false statement.
28	//
29	// The history index already solves this and its wording is the model:
30	//
31	//	history index size does not match the manifest; run `entire brain refresh
32	//	history` to rebuild it
33	//
34	// Note WHERE that check lives. It is not inside the per-record reader; it is
35	// in the function that loads the artifact the manifest declares, so every
36	// caller of that artifact inherits it and the REBUILD path — which must be
37	// able to run against the damaged artifact — does not. Facts need the same
38	// shape, and Load is the wrong seam for three reasons:
39	//
40	//  1. Load is per-branch and the manifest records only a total across
41	//     branches, so Load cannot know what N is for the branch it is
42	//     reading.
43	//  2. Its ~30 callers include distill, remember, facts gc/promote/merge and
44	//     refresh — the very commands that REPAIR a lossy store. A loader that
45	//     failed closed would wedge the store shut with no way out.
46	//  3. The manifest's count is produced from the same folded read Load serves
47	//     (see updateFactSourceManifestLocked). Checking the claim with the same
48	//     view that produced it makes the check an exact inverse: any
49	//     disagreement is real.
50	//
51	// So the check lives here, beside MissingBranchStores — the existing seam
52	// for "the manifest names something the store cannot produce" — and every
53	// surface reads one report. The retrieval note inherits through the single
54	// emptyResultBlindSpot choke point, which covers recall, search, query and
55	// retrieve at once.
56	
57	// COUNTS ARE NOT ENOUGH. The first cut of this check compared Declared against
58	// Readable and nothing else, which leaves a corruption that PRESERVES the count
59	// completely invisible: overwrite one line of facts.ndjson with a copy of
60	// another and the store still yields N records, still parses, still declares N
61	// — and the fact whose line was taken is gone. `get fact:<id>` says "not
62	// found", doctor says "facts: ok", and `search` goes back to volunteering that
63	// the answer "may genuinely not be in the brain". That is the same affirmative
64	// false statement this file exists to eliminate, reached by a different route.
65	//
66	// The obvious repair — compare the declared id SET against the readable one —
67	// is not available: sources.facts records counts (facts/distilled/authored/
68	// superseded/by_kind), never ids, and putting ids there would not help. That
69	// manifest is re-derived from the store itself by SummarizeSource on every
70	// mutating remember, refresh, gc, promote and retract, so a declared id set would
71	// re-baseline onto the damage at the next write exactly as the count does, and
72	// would cry loss on every legitimate id-changing operation in between.
73	//
74	// What IS checkable from the store alone, with no bookkeeping and nothing that
75	// can go stale, is the invariant the store is written under: WITHIN ONE BRANCH
76	// AN ID IDENTIFIES EXACTLY ONE FACT. Every writer keys by id before it writes
77	// (factmerge.Upsert, factmerge.Promote via IndexOf, factmerge.GC), so a branch
78	// that yields the same id twice was not written by this program. The second
79	// record did not join the fact set; it stands where a different fact used to
80	// be. That is loss, and it is loss the count cannot see.
81	//
82	// Per BRANCH, emphatically not per brain. A fact id is sha256 of normalized
83	// text plus sorted paths (factmerge.RecordID) — the branch is not in it — so
84	// the same fact carried between branches keeps its id, which is precisely what
85	// `facts promote` does on purpose. A brain-wide id set would report data loss
86	// on every promote, and a check that cries loss on a legitimate operation is
87	// worse than the hole it closes.
88	
89	// DefectMode names WHICH way the store fails the manifest. They are
90	// different user situations and must not collapse into one sentence: "not
91	// built" is a rebuild, "corrupt" is a repair, "lossy" is data that is gone and
92	// has to be re-distilled, and "duplicated" is data that was overwritten while
93	// the numbers stayed right.
94	type DefectMode string
95	
96	const (
97		// DefectNone is a store that can produce what the manifest declares.
98		DefectNone DefectMode = ""
99		// DefectMissing: a declared branch has no facts.ndjson at all.
100		// Already detected by MissingBranchStores; kept in its own words.
101		DefectMissing DefectMode = "missing"
102		// DefectUnreadable: a line will not parse. The store is corrupt
103		// and nothing on the branch can be read, not just the bad line.
104		DefectUnreadable DefectMode = "unreadable"
105		// DefectLossy: every line parses, but the store yields fewer
106		// facts than the manifest declares. This is the readable-but-short case —
107		// the one that used to pass every health surface.
108		DefectLossy DefectMode = "lossy"
109		// DefectStale: the store yields MORE facts than the manifest
110		// declares. Not data loss — the manifest is behind — but still a declared
111		// number that was never observed, so it is reported rather than printed.
112		DefectStale DefectMode = "stale"
113		// DefectDuplicated: every line parses and the counts are not
114		// short, but one branch stores the same fact id twice. Deliberately NOT
115		// folded into "lossy": lossy is a SHORTFALL — fewer facts than claimed,
116		// repaired by re-distilling what is missing — while this is a
117		// SUBSTITUTION, where the arithmetic is intact and a specific fact was
118		// overwritten by a copy of its neighbour. Telling the two apart is the
119		// difference between "some of your memory did not survive" and "this
120		// particular record is standing in for one that is gone".
121		DefectDuplicated DefectMode = "duplicated"
122	)
123	
124	// Integrity is the cross-check result. The zero value is a healthy
125	// store, so callers may use it unconditionally.
126	type Integrity struct {
127		// Declared is sources.facts.facts — what the manifest claims.
128		Declared int `json:"declared"`
129		// Readable is how many records the store actually yields that are facts:
130		// a record carrying an id. A line that parses as JSON but has no id (the
131		// canonical corruption in this defect) is counted in Unusable, never here,
132		// because it is unaddressable by `get`, invisible to recall, and dropped
133		// by every status/scope filter.
134		Readable int `json:"readable"`
135		// Pending is sources.facts.pending_reconcile — staged candidate records
136		// the manifest deliberately declares OUTSIDE Facts (SummarizeSource
137		// books a factmerge.StatusCandidate under its own counter until the next
138		// distill reconciles it). The store yields those records, so every
139		// Readable-vs-Declared comparison must add Pending back or a brain with
140		// one staged candidate reports "the manifest is behind the store"
141		// forever, through the very refresh the warning recommends.
142		Pending int `json:"pending,omitempty"`
143		// Unusable counts records read from the store that carry no id. They are
144		// reported even when the counts happen to agree, because a manifest
145		// re-summarized from an already-damaged store would otherwise hide them.
146		Unusable int `json:"unusable,omitempty"`
147		// Distinct is how many DIFFERENT fact ids the store yields, summed across
148		// branches but counted within each one (a fact id does not include the
149		// branch, so `facts promote` legitimately stores one id on two branches —
150		// see the file header). In a store this program wrote, Distinct always
151		// equals Readable; anything less is a record that overwrote another.
152		Distinct int `json:"distinct,omitempty"`
153		// DuplicateIDs names the ids a single branch stores more than once, sorted
154		// so the report is stable. The full set is kept for JSON readers;
155		// the one-line warning names only the first few.
156		DuplicateIDs []string `json:"duplicate_ids,omitempty"`
157		// Missing names declared branches whose facts.ndjson is absent.
158		Missing []string `json:"missing_branches,omitempty"`
159		// ParseError is the first line the store could not parse, in the loader's
160		// own words ("parse facts.ndjson line 3: ...").
161		ParseError string `json:"parse_error,omitempty"`
162		// Unreadable names legacy branch stores that will not parse. The flat
163		// store has no per-branch attribution; the field survives for JSON readers
164		// and for ParseError context.
165		Unreadable []string `json:"unreadable_branches,omitempty"`
166		// Mode is the classification; empty when the store is intact.
167		Mode DefectMode `json:"mode,omitempty"`
168	}

171	func (r Integrity) OK() bool { return r.Mode == DefectNone }
172	
173	// pendingClause names the staged-candidate share of the expected count, so a
174	// mismatch message whose arithmetic includes Pending still adds up on the page.
175	func (r Integrity) pendingClause() string {
176		if r.Pending == 0 {
177			return ""
178		}
179		return fmt.Sprintf(" (+%d staged candidate(s))", r.Pending)
180	}
181

183	// staged candidates awaiting reconciliation. It is what the store must yield
184	// for the cross-check to call it intact.
185	func (r Integrity) expected() int { return r.Declared + r.Pending }
186	
187	// Lost is how many declared facts the store cannot produce. Zero unless the
188	// store is short.
189	func (r Integrity) Lost() int {
190		if r.expected() > r.Readable {
191			return r.expected() - r.Readable
192		}
193		return 0
194	}
195

197	// id. Zero unless a branch repeated an id.

200	// manifest's COUNT, and a substitution is invisible to that measurement by
201	// construction: the count is exactly what the corruption preserved.
202	func (r Integrity) Overwritten() int {
203		if r.Readable > r.Distinct {
204			return r.Readable - r.Distinct

206		return 0
207	}

216	// stopped where the list did.
217	func factStoreIDList(ids []string) string {
218		if len(ids) <= factStoreDuplicateIDsShown {
219			return strings.Join(ids, ", ")
220		}
221		return fmt.Sprintf("%s and %d more",
222			strings.Join(ids[:factStoreDuplicateIDsShown], ", "),
223			len(ids)-factStoreDuplicateIDsShown,
224		)
225	}

227	// RepairHint is the repair for a store that lost content. Rebuilding the
228	// manifest alone would only re-baseline the loss, so the fact commands' own
229	// wording — refresh, then re-distill — is what gets named.
230	func RepairHint() string {
231		return "run `" + base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "refresh") + "` and re-distill"
232	}

235	// intact. Each mode keeps its own words.
236	func (r Integrity) Warning() string {
237		switch r.Mode {
238		case DefectMissing:
239			return "the manifest declares memories but no memory store (" + RepositoryPath + ") is on disk; they cannot be recalled — run `" + base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "refresh") + "` and re-distill"
240		case DefectUnreadable:
241			where := "memory store"

243				where = "memory store for " + strings.Join(r.Unreadable, ", ")
244			}
245			return fmt.Sprintf(

247				where, r.ParseError, r.Declared, RepairHint(),
248			)
249		case DefectLossy:

253			)
254			if lost := r.Lost(); lost > 0 {

256			}
257			if r.Unusable > 0 {

259			}

262			// it is not one of the ones the arithmetic accounted for.
263			if overwritten := r.Overwritten(); overwritten > 0 {
264				detail += fmt.Sprintf("; %d more record(s) repeat a memory id (%s)", overwritten, factStoreIDList(r.DuplicateIDs))

267		case DefectDuplicated:
268			return fmt.Sprintf(

271			)

319			}

16	// distillCoverage reports the last recorded distillation and sessions created
17	// since it. Older sessions may also be unprocessed; timestamps do not prove coverage.
18	func distillCoverage(manifest *exportManifest) (last time.Time, undigested int, ok bool) {
19		if manifest == nil || manifest.Sources == nil || manifest.Sources.Facts == nil {
20			return time.Time{}, 0, false
21		}
22		last = manifest.Sources.Facts.LastDistilledAt
23		if last.IsZero() {
24			return time.Time{}, 0, false
25		}
26		if manifest.Sources.Sessions != nil {
27			for _, s := range manifest.Sources.Sessions.Sessions {
28				if s.CreatedAt.After(last) {
29					undigested++
30				}
31			}
32		}
33		return last, undigested, true
34	}
35	
36	// emptyResultBlindSpot is the one-liner appended to empty retrieval results.
37	// Reads the manifest and, when facts are declared, cross-checks the fact store
38	// behind it. Both are cheap, and this only runs on an EMPTY result — the exact
39	// moment the difference between "nothing was stored" and "what was stored is
40	// gone" decides whether the line is true.
41	// Empty string when nothing useful can be said (no manifest at all).
42	func emptyResultBlindSpot(brainDir string) string {
43		return emptyResultBlindSpotOnBranch(brainDir, "")
44	}
45	
46	// emptyResultBlindSpotOnBranch is emptyResultBlindSpot for callers that know
47	// which branch they queried. Facts are stored per branch, so "nothing here" and
48	// "nothing anywhere" are different answers and only this variant can tell them
49	// apart.
50	func emptyResultBlindSpotOnBranch(brainDir, branch string) string {
51		manifest, err := bmanifest.Load(brainDir)
52		// A missing manifest loads as an empty struct, not an error, and a nil
53		// Sources is exactly that case: bmanifest.Normalize gives every manifest
54		// it actually parsed a non-nil Sources, so only the absent-manifest path
55		// reaches here with nil. That is the NO-BRAIN case, and it is the one this
56		// line most needs to cover — see noBrainBlindSpot.
57		if err != nil || manifest == nil || manifest.Sources == nil {
58			return noBrainBlindSpot(err)
59		}
60		// Every branch below EXPLAINS an absence, and each explanation is false
61		// when the facts were stored and the store lost them. The last one —
62		// "the answer may genuinely not be in the brain" — is the most damaging
63		// thing this tool can say: it tells a user their memory never existed,
64		// immediately after it was destroyed. A known-lossy store must never reach
65		// it, so the truth replaces the note here.
66		//
67		// This single choke point is why recall, search, query and retrieve all
68		// inherit the correction without each having to remember to ask.
69		if integrity := factstore.Inspect(brainDir, manifest.Sources.Facts); !integrity.OK() {
70			return "note: this empty result is NOT evidence of absence — " + integrity.Warning()
71		}
72		// A connected repo whose branch never synced may be missing the whole
73		// team's facts, and the remedy is one command — more actionable than "try
74		// another branch", so it wins over the branch note below. The integrity
75		// check above still wins: a store that lost facts is not merely unsynced.
76		if note := unsyncedHostedFactsBlindSpot(brainDir, branch); note != "" {
77			return note
78		}
79		// Facts are recorded against the branch the session ran on. Sessions run on
80		// feature branches and queries run from main, so an empty result on one
81		// branch is the ordinary case rather than a signal about the corpus.
82		//
83		// THIS IS CHECKED BEFORE THE COVERAGE NOTES, and the order is the whole
84		// point. Both can be true at once, and when they are, naming the branch
85		// that holds the facts is the only one the caller can act on: it ends with
86		// a flag they can retype, where "coverage of older sessions is unknown"
87		// ends with nothing to do.
88		//
89		// Checked last, this feature was unreachable in the case it was built for.
90		// `undigested > 0` is true in every repository where a session has been
91		// captured since the last distillation -- which is every actively worked
92		// repository, and you are on a feature branch BECAUSE you have been
93		// working. The fixtures never caught it because they set LastDistilledAt
94		// to now with sessions two hours old, so undigested was always 0 and the
95		// branch path was never exercised.
96		//
97		// An import with --overwrite replaced the fact layer wholesale, so facts
98		// remembered here before it are gone. Every note below this point talks
99		// about distillation coverage, which would send the reader to re-distill --
100		// and re-distilling cannot bring back what an import replaced. Ordered
101		// after the integrity and branch checks: a lost store or a wrong branch is
102		// still the more precise answer when either applies.
103		importedAt, imported := lastBundleImportAt(brainDir)
104		last, undigested, ok := distillCoverage(manifest)
105		// Only while the import is still the most recent thing that happened. It
106		// stays TRUE forever -- those facts really are gone -- but it stops being
107		// the most useful answer once work has been distilled since, and returning
108		// it unconditionally masked coverage information permanently. Raised as a
109		// finding, and correct.
110		if imported && (!ok || importedAt.After(last)) {
111			return fmt.Sprintf("note: a bundle import on %s replaced this brain's memory layer with the bundle's, so memories recorded here before then are no longer present; this empty result is not evidence of absence", importedAt.Format("2006-01-02"))
112		}
113		// Past that point the coverage note leads, but the import is still named:
114		// re-distilling cannot bring back what the import replaced, and a reader
115		// sent to distill without being told that would try it and find nothing.
116		suffix := ""
117		if imported {
118			suffix = fmt.Sprintf(" (a bundle import on %s replaced the fact layer; anything recorded before then is gone whatever distillation reports)", importedAt.Format("2006-01-02"))
119		}
120		if !ok {
121			if manifest.Sources.Sessions != nil && len(manifest.Sources.Sessions.Sessions) > 0 {
122				return fmt.Sprintf("note: distillation coverage is unknown for %d captured session(s); run `"+base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "distill")+"`", len(manifest.Sources.Sessions.Sessions)) + suffix
123			}
124			return "note: no distillation timestamp is recorded; run `" + base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "refresh") + "`, then `distill`" + suffix
125		}
126		if undigested > 0 {
127			return fmt.Sprintf("note: last distillation %s; %d session(s) captured since; coverage of older sessions is unknown", last.Format("2006-01-02"), undigested) + suffix
128		}
129		return fmt.Sprintf("note: last distillation %s; complete session coverage is unknown, so this empty result is not evidence of absence", last.Format("2006-01-02")) + suffix
130	}
131	
132	// otherBranchBlindSpot moved to factstore.OtherBranchBlindSpot with the
133	// extracted command surface; get's miss note shares it from there.
134	
135	// noBrainBlindSpot is the note for a repository whose brain does not exist or
136	// cannot be read.
137	//
138	// This case used to return the empty string — "nothing useful to say" — which
139	// inverted the whole point of the mechanism. A brain that HAS been built got a
140	// note explaining its empty result; a repository with no brain at all got a
141	// bare
142	//
143	//	{"branch":"main","query":"Hello","results":[]}
144	//
145	// so the note appeared when it was least needed and was missing when it
146	// mattered most. An agent reads that empty array as "the brain knows nothing
147	// about this" and writes the tool off, when the true answer is "there is no
148	// brain here yet". brain_code already refuses this state out loud ("semantic
149	// index missing", naming the refresh command that builds one); the text
150	// retrieval surface stayed silent about it.
151	//
152	// Same mechanism as every other line in this file: one `note:` string, carried
153	// by the existing blind_spot field on JSON responses and printed under the
154	// "no results" line on text ones. Nothing new is introduced.
155	func noBrainBlindSpot(loadErr error) string {
156		if loadErr != nil {
157			return "note: this repository's brain could not be read, so this empty result is not evidence of absence; run `" + base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "status") + "` for the reason"
158		}
159		return "note: no brain has been built for this repository, so nothing is indexed here and this empty result is not evidence of absence; run `" + base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "setup") + "`"
160	}
161	
162	// otherBranchSessionBlindSpot reports captured sessions held on branches other
163	// than the one scanned. It is the SESSION-unit twin of otherBranchBlindSpot.
164	//
165	// Evidence recall scans canonical sessions on one branch and returns spans, not
166	// facts. Reusing the fact note here would attach "N active fact(s) on M other
167	// branch(es)" to a result that is not about facts -- a note that does not match
168	// the shape of the answer is the hazard the review named on the unified
169	// surfaces, and it applies just as much to this one.
170	//
171	// So the discipline is the same and the unit is the result's own: an empty
172	// evidence result on a branch holding no sessions, while other branches hold
173	// them, is the same wrong-branch trap and the same actionable remedy.
174	//
175	// Empty when the caller did not say which branch it scanned, when the manifest
176	// cannot be read, or when no other branch holds a session.
177	func otherBranchSessionBlindSpot(brainDir, branch string) string {
178		branch = strings.TrimSpace(branch)
179		if branch == "" {
180			return ""
181		}
182		manifest, err := bmanifest.Load(brainDir)
183		if err != nil || manifest == nil || manifest.Sources == nil || manifest.Sources.Sessions == nil {
184			return ""
185		}
186		byBranch := map[string]int{}
187		here := 0
188		for _, session := range manifest.Sources.Sessions.Sessions {
189			name := strings.TrimSpace(session.Branch)
190			if name == "" {
191				continue
192			}
193			if name == branch {
194				here++
195				continue
196			}
197			byBranch[name]++
198		}
199		// Sessions on THIS branch mean the scan had material to work with, so an
200		// empty result is about the query, not the branch.
201		if here > 0 || len(byBranch) == 0 {
202			return ""
203		}
204		total := 0
205		names := make([]string, 0, len(byBranch))
206		for name, n := range byBranch {
207			total += n
208			names = append(names, name)
209		}
210		// Map iteration is randomised, so an unsorted list would differ between
211		// identical runs.
212		sort.Strings(names)
213		return fmt.Sprintf(
214			"note: no sessions were captured on %s; %d session(s) on %d other branch(es): %s — retry with --branch <name>",
215			branch, total, len(names), strings.Join(names, ", "))
216	}
217	
218	// unsyncedHostedFactsBlindSpot notes a branch that has not synced against the
219	// CONNECTED hosted brain: repo-level hosted.json present, per-branch
220	// hosted-target.json absent or recording a different target (a marker left by
221	// a previous connection must not suppress the note). Purely local reads; no
222	// network.
223	func unsyncedHostedFactsBlindSpot(brainDir, branch string) string {
224		// The branchless surface (emptyResultBlindSpot) passes ""; facts sync per
225		// branch, so there is no empty-branch marker and the note would be
226		// nonsense — and would hide the coverage notes below it.
227		if strings.TrimSpace(branch) == "" {
228			return ""
229		}
230		binding, connected, err := brainstore.ReadHostedRepoBinding(brainDir)
231		if err != nil || !connected || binding.OptedOut {
232			return ""
233		}
234		if checkHostedFactsBinding(brainDir, binding.RepoID, binding.BaseURL) == nil {
235			return ""
236		}
237		// The remedy must be a command that PULLS: `facts sync` only publishes
238		// (and would write the marker that silences this note without fetching
239		// anything); connect runs the full sync-and-pull.
240		return "note: this repository is connected to a hosted brain but has not synced with it; run '" + base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "connect") + "' or wait for the next daemon tick"
241	}

102		// still the more precise answer when either applies.
103		importedAt, imported := lastBundleImportAt(brainDir)
104		last, undigested, ok := distillCoverage(manifest)
105		// Only while the import is still the most recent thing that happened. It
106		// stays TRUE forever -- those facts really are gone -- but it stops being
107		// the most useful answer once work has been distilled since, and returning
108		// it unconditionally masked coverage information permanently. Raised as a
109		// finding, and correct.
110		if imported && (!ok || importedAt.After(last)) {
111			return fmt.Sprintf("note: a bundle import on %s replaced this brain's memory layer with the bundle's, so memories recorded here before then are no longer present; this empty result is not evidence of absence", importedAt.Format("2006-01-02"))
112		}
113		// Past that point the coverage note leads, but the import is still named:
114		// re-distilling cannot bring back what the import replaced, and a reader
115		// sent to distill without being told that would try it and find nothing.
116		suffix := ""
117		if imported {
118			suffix = fmt.Sprintf(" (a bundle import on %s replaced the fact layer; anything recorded before then is gone whatever distillation reports)", importedAt.Format("2006-01-02"))
119		}
120		if !ok {
121			if manifest.Sources.Sessions != nil && len(manifest.Sources.Sessions.Sessions) > 0 {
122				return fmt.Sprintf("note: distillation coverage is unknown for %d captured session(s); run `"+base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "distill")+"`", len(manifest.Sources.Sessions.Sessions)) + suffix
123			}
124			return "note: no distillation timestamp is recorded; run `" + base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "refresh") + "`, then `distill`" + suffix
125		}
126		if undigested > 0 {
127			return fmt.Sprintf("note: last distillation %s; %d session(s) captured since; coverage of older sessions is unknown", last.Format("2006-01-02"), undigested) + suffix
128		}
129		return fmt.Sprintf("note: last distillation %s; complete session coverage is unknown, so this empty result is not evidence of absence", last.Format("2006-01-02")) + suffix
130	}
131	
132	// otherBranchBlindSpot moved to factstore.OtherBranchBlindSpot with the
133	// extracted command surface; get's miss note shares it from there.
134	
135	// noBrainBlindSpot is the note for a repository whose brain does not exist or
136	// cannot be read.
137	//
138	// This case used to return the empty string — "nothing useful to say" — which
139	// inverted the whole point of the mechanism. A brain that HAS been built got a
140	// note explaining its empty result; a repository with no brain at all got a
141	// bare
142	//
143	//	{"branch":"main","query":"Hello","results":[]}
144	//
145	// so the note appeared when it was least needed and was missing when it
146	// mattered most. An agent reads that empty array as "the brain knows nothing
147	// about this" and writes the tool off, when the true answer is "there is no
148	// brain here yet". brain_code already refuses this state out loud ("semantic
149	// index missing", naming the refresh command that builds one); the text
150	// retrieval surface stayed silent about it.
151	//
152	// Same mechanism as every other line in this file: one `note:` string, carried
153	// by the existing blind_spot field on JSON responses and printed under the
154	// "no results" line on text ones. Nothing new is introduced.
155	func noBrainBlindSpot(loadErr error) string {
156		if loadErr != nil {
157			return "note: this repository's brain could not be read, so this empty result is not evidence of absence; run `" + base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "status") + "` for the reason"
158		}
159		return "note: no brain has been built for this repository, so nothing is indexed here and this empty result is not evidence of absence; run `" + base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "setup") + "`"
160	}
161	
162	// otherBranchSessionBlindSpot reports captured sessions held on branches other
163	// than the one scanned. It is the SESSION-unit twin of otherBranchBlindSpot.
164	//
165	// Evidence recall scans canonical sessions on one branch and returns spans, not
166	// facts. Reusing the fact note here would attach "N active fact(s) on M other
167	// branch(es)" to a result that is not about facts -- a note that does not match
168	// the shape of the answer is the hazard the review named on the unified
169	// surfaces, and it applies just as much to this one.
170	//
171	// So the discipline is the same and the unit is the result's own: an empty
172	// evidence result on a branch holding no sessions, while other branches hold
173	// them, is the same wrong-branch trap and the same actionable remedy.
174	//
175	// Empty when the caller did not say which branch it scanned, when the manifest
176	// cannot be read, or when no other branch holds a session.
177	func otherBranchSessionBlindSpot(brainDir, branch string) string {
178		branch = strings.TrimSpace(branch)
179		if branch == "" {
180			return ""
181		}
182		manifest, err := bmanifest.Load(brainDir)
183		if err != nil || manifest == nil || manifest.Sources == nil || manifest.Sources.Sessions == nil {
184			return ""
185		}
186		byBranch := map[string]int{}
187		here := 0
188		for _, session := range manifest.Sources.Sessions.Sessions {
189			name := strings.TrimSpace(session.Branch)
190			if name == "" {
191				continue
192			}
193			if name == branch {
194				here++
195				continue
196			}
197			byBranch[name]++
198		}
199		// Sessions on THIS branch mean the scan had material to work with, so an
200		// empty result is about the query, not the branch.
201		if here > 0 || len(byBranch) == 0 {
202			return ""
203		}
204		total := 0
205		names := make([]string, 0, len(byBranch))
206		for name, n := range byBranch {
207			total += n
208			names = append(names, name)
209		}
210		// Map iteration is randomised, so an unsorted list would differ between
211		// identical runs.
212		sort.Strings(names)
213		return fmt.Sprintf(
214			"note: no sessions were captured on %s; %d session(s) on %d other branch(es): %s — retry with --branch <name>",
215			branch, total, len(names), strings.Join(names, ", "))
216	}
217	
218	// unsyncedHostedFactsBlindSpot notes a branch that has not synced against the
219	// CONNECTED hosted brain: repo-level hosted.json present, per-branch
220	// hosted-target.json absent or recording a different target (a marker left by
221	// a previous connection must not suppress the note). Purely local reads; no
222	// network.
223	func unsyncedHostedFactsBlindSpot(brainDir, branch string) string {
224		// The branchless surface (emptyResultBlindSpot) passes ""; facts sync per
225		// branch, so there is no empty-branch marker and the note would be
226		// nonsense — and would hide the coverage notes below it.
227		if strings.TrimSpace(branch) == "" {
228			return ""
229		}
230		binding, connected, err := brainstore.ReadHostedRepoBinding(brainDir)
231		if err != nil || !connected || binding.OptedOut {
232			return ""
233		}
234		if checkHostedFactsBinding(brainDir, binding.RepoID, binding.BaseURL) == nil {
235			return ""
236		}
237		// The remedy must be a command that PULLS: `facts sync` only publishes
238		// (and would write the marker that silences this note without fetching
239		// anything); connect runs the full sync-and-pull.
240		return "note: this repository is connected to a hosted brain but has not synced with it; run '" + base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "connect") + "' or wait for the next daemon tick"
241	}

- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. content.text:
The biggest problem is the data on disk, not the ranker. Your live brain was never migrated, so the "24,700 facts" are really about 2,834 unique facts (2,811 active), each copied many times across 176 per-branch files. Every hot command re-reads all of those copies on each call. Both warnings come from setup problems rather than real data loss. Findings, most valuable first:

**1. The fact store was never migrated, and "24k facts" is mostly copies.**
- The live brain at `~/.local/share/entire/plugins/data/brain/repos/gh/entireio/entire-brain/facts/` has no `store.json`. It still uses the old layout: 176 `<branch>/facts.ndjson` files, 24,735 lines, 23 MB.
- Those lines hold only 2,834 distinct ids. 878 ids appear in 16 files each.
- Every `factstore.Load` reads the folder, then parses and merges all 24,735 lines (`repo_fact_compat.go:82-186`).
- The binary you run (`~/.local/bin/entire-brain`, built Oct 25, version `dev`) is older than the flat store (commit 73b62b21, Nov 2), so its `refresh` never migrates.
- A current build migrates on refresh (`reclassifyAllFactsContext` → `migrateFactStoreLocked`, `facts_manifest.go:48`). The manifest would then declare about 2.8k facts.
- **So what:** rebuilding and running `refresh` once cuts every fact read about 9x and makes the fact count honest. This is the cheapest big win.

**2. The manifest mismatch is 7 staged candidates that your binary doesn't count.**
- The manifest says `facts: 24728, pending_reconcile: 7`, and 24728 + 7 = 24735 readable. The 7 records have `status: candidate`.
- Current code adds pending candidates to the expected count (`integrity.go:185`, fix 98a7c172 on Oct 26). Your Oct 25 binary doesn't.
- Only `distill` reconciles candidates. `refresh` never runs distill (`refresh.go:490-524`), and the last distill was Oct 22.
- No watcher is running: no `entire-brain` process and no LaunchAgent. In practice refresh is manual-only here.
- A second drift source exists in current code: distill writes the store mid-run every 50 calls (`distill_cmd.go:73`, `:1194`) but only updates the manifest at the end (`:1500-1548`). A killed distill leaves the store ahead of the manifest.
- **So what:** the warning is a false alarm on an old build. Separately, mid-run flushes should also update `sources.facts`.

**3. "Seed is stale" can't be fixed by refreshing, given how the brain is shared.**
- The seed counts as fresh only if its commit equals HEAD (`refresh.go:1039-1058`, status at `agent_surface.go:4713`).
- One brain is keyed by the origin remote (`env.go:204`, `git remote get-url origin`) and shared by all 8 worktrees, each with its own HEAD.
- The seed is at 92333786, from Oct 27. At most one worktree can ever match.
- **So what:** the warning is permanent noise for multi-worktree users. Consider an "ancestor of HEAD within N commits" check or a per-worktree seed.

**4. `recall` has no fact index and reads the whole store up to three times per query.**
- `facts_read_cmd.go:103` does `factstore.Load` (full merge).
- `:137` loads the 1.8 MB manifest, then `InspectBrain` loads it again and calls `loadCombined` again (`integrity.go:298,354`). That is a second full merge.
- If the result is empty, `EmptyResultBlindSpot` loads the manifest and merges the store a third time (`blind_spot.go:51,69`).
- BM25 is computed per query over every candidate, with no stored index. `newBM25Corpus` re-tokenizes every fact twice (plain, plus normalized/CJK) and rebuilds document frequencies. `bm25Score` allocates a term-count map per document (`facts_bm25.go:138-196`). The code comment says this was measured at 1,209 facts.
- There are also about 4 git subprocesses per recall: toplevel, remote, `branch --show-current`, and `rev-parse HEAD` for the receipt (`facts_vitality.go:324`).
- The `sqlite_driver` in the capabilities report is only for the history and doc FTS indexes (`history_fts.go`, `index-fts.sqlite` 204 MB). Facts never touch SQLite.
- Nothing is cached between invocations.
- **So what:** have `Load` and `Inspect` share one merge, and keep a stored token/postings sidecar or an FTS5 table keyed by the store's digest.

**5. `brief` runs the full, non-lightweight status, and reads the fact store twice.**
- `agent_surface.go:1464` calls `buildBrainStatusReport` with `lightweight=false` (`:4508`). That includes:
  - the manifest
  - a `fetchGraphStore` subprocess (`:4575`)
  - `factstore.Inspect`, a full merge (`:4624`)
  - live git state
  - the retrieval audit
  - `semanticFreshnessReport(audit=true)` (`:4669`)
  - onboarding
- Then brief does a second graph subprocess (`fetchGraphTaskContext`, `:1505`), history FTS (`:1620`, which is fine), the raw history walk (`:1705`), and `factstore.Load` plus BM25 again (`:1734-1753`).
- It then loads patterns, consolidations and themes (`:1808-1831`) and may make git-intent calls.
- For some task wordings it also reads up to 2,500 repo files (`:2856`).
- **So what:** brief is the slowest hot path. Use lightweight status and reuse the facts it already loaded.

**6. Brief's raw "history" scan reads derived indexes, and its hits outrank the FTS-ranked history.**
- The raw walk covers the whole brain directory (`agent_surface.go:5306`). It skips history, facts, patterns, seed, semantic, export and locks (`:5023-5040`), but not `docs/` or `entities/`.
- `sessions/` is empty in this brain, so the "raw history" hits come from `docs/index.json` (1.5 MB, the derived doc index) and `entities/index.json` (520 KB on a single line, which matches almost any identifier).
- `mergeBrainBriefHistoryMatches(limit, rawMatches, indexedMatches)` puts raw hits first (`:1709`, `:5495`), so they push out ranked history.
- The scan runs even when the indexed results already fill the limit, because it is passed `nil` as the existing matches.
- Hardcoded tweaks look tuned to an eval: an "ultron" exclusion and a +100 boost for queries containing LIMIT (`:5443`, `:5476`).
- **So what:** this is a quality bug in brief's history section. Skip derived directories and merge indexed results first.

**7. Recall's arms, from `facts_commands.go:21-33`:**

| Arm | What it adds | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Ranking (`rankFacts`) | BM25, plus +8 per locus overlap and +4 for closed-negative facts (`facts_bm25.go:202-214`) | The +4 applies to about 17% of facts on any match, regardless of relevance. Questionable. |
| Proposal (`UpdateFactSourceManifest*`) | Write side only | The proposal framework was removed (`guard.go:33-34`). This is leftover. |
| Receipt (`RecordServedFacts`) | A `git rev-parse HEAD` subprocess plus an append to `vitality.ndjson` under a lock | Paid on every recall, but by design it never affects ranking (`facts_vitality.go:27`). Cost with no benefit today. |
| Blind-spot | Explanatory note | Only on empty results, but merges the whole store again. |
| Evidence (`--evidence`, opt-in) | Loads all facts and runs BM25 just to get session anchors, then reads up to 128 transcripts / 32 MiB raw | Takes sessions in manifest order, not most recent; substring scoring (`recall_evidence_source.go:238-330`). Expensive. |
| Query expansion (`--expand`, opt-in) | Spawns an LLM agent CLI | Its cache path is `""`, so results are never saved (`facts_commands.go:82`, `facts_expand.go:74`). Full LLM latency on every call. |

**8. There are no quality filters at recall time, beyond "active" plus optional scope/kind/locus.**
- Dedup is exact only: the id is a sha256 of the normalized text plus paths (`factmerge/record.go:26-28`).
- Near-duplicates and conflicts are judged by the LLM during distill. Below the confidence threshold, both facts stay active and are linked via RelatedIDs (`factmerge/merge.go:40-46`). 1,910 active records in the live store carry related_ids, so unresolved pairs reach recall.
- `confidence` is "1.00" on 23,404 of 24,586 active records, so it carries no signal.
- There is no aging or decay. Recency weighting is opt-in and only on unified search/query (`retrieve.go:189`, `recency.go:66`, 90-day half-life). `recall` doesn't use it at all.
- Locus drift only adds an annotation (`guard.go:79`).
- **So what:** the best quality levers are collapsing RelatedIDs pairs into one result, a default recency prior, and feeding the vitality data into ranking.

**9. Refresh is partly incremental, but the fact and doc steps rebuild everything.**
- History is rebuilt only when it's not current (`refresh.go:336`). Seed is gated on the commit, and the code index on `semanticRefreshNeeded`.
- The doc index rebuilds on every refresh, because `historyIndex` defaults to true (`refresh.go:118`, `:367`).
- The mirror and reclassify steps each do a full Load and Write. `updateFactSourceManifestLocked` then loads the store again (`facts_manifest.go:89-95`). That is 3-4 full store reads plus a whole-file rewrite (`repo_fact_store.go:147-167`) per refresh.
- `watch` does a cheap update every 5 minutes and a full refresh at most every 30 minutes, triggered by a fingerprint (`watch.go:96-101`, `:119-133`).
- But the full refresh is deferred whenever the worktree has uncommitted changes (`watch.go:406`). In always-dirty Conductor workspaces, it effectively never runs.

**10. Small leftovers in the hot paths.**
- `AnnotateUnifiedFactResults` builds a lookup map over the whole corpus for every query (`guard.go:39-42`).
- A dead `docs/embeddings/vectors.bin` (967 KB) is left over from the removed semantic retrieval.
- A `quarantine-stray-facts-*` directory sits at the brain root.
- **So what:** cleanup. Fine once the corpus is about 2.8k facts.

**Suggested order:** rebuild the binary and run `refresh` (fixes 1 and 2), stop merging the store repeatedly in recall and brief (4, 5), fix the brief raw-scan skip list and merge order (6), then make seed staleness worktree-aware (3).
